extracted.intended_audience: physicians, surgeons, anatomists, and natural philosophers (17th-century medical/scientific readership)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing and reporting anatomical dissections, surgical trials, and clinical case accounts that document procedures, observations, and experimental tests. Emphasis on procedural detail, quantitative measures, comparative (animal/human) observations, and links between clinical signs and post-mortem anatomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid immediate suturing after suspected venomous dog bite
rubrics_metrics.description: When treating a child bitten by a dog: 'The wound was treated with digestives for some time, sutures were forborn, though otherwise necessary, that the venom might be more freely discharged.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not suture initially if venom discharge is desired; apply digestive/expectoration-promoting treatments, allow free discharge of pus/venom, and monitor wound healing and systemic signs before closing. Record evolution of local infection and systemic symptoms (fever, delirium, convulsions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose animal models proportional to humans for styptic testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of common practice: 'pretenders to such remedies have made choice of younger animals, as dogs and calves, &c. ... we ought to make our experiments on those animals whose size and age bear a proportion to it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select experimental animals whose size and age approximate human physiology when testing hemostatic agents; justify model choice because arterial blood flow and vessel thickness vary with bulk and age (foetal arteries thinner, aged arteries thicker/cartilaginous), which affects translational relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human clinical success is the ultimate standard for styptics
rubrics_metrics.description: 'since the only standard of their use is their success on the human body, we ought to make our experiments on those animals whose size and age bear a proportion to it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate styptic/hemostatic remedies primarily by documented outcomes in human patients; animal trials are supportive but cannot replace human efficacy and safety data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report and evaluate adverse effects in human applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Observed harms after human use of a styptic: 'intolerable pains ... large eschars, and so horrid an appearance; which sufficiently proved that this vulnerary powder is a violent caustic.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record and report delayed bleeding, severe pain, formation of large eschars, and any tissue necrosis following application; interpret such signs as evidence of causticity and potential contraindication for human use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise surgical caution during paracentesis to avoid intestinal puncture
rubrics_metrics.description: 'I remember it was the fear of this that once retarded an eminent physician from a paracentesis upon his patient, lest the surgeon in making perforation should puncture the intestines.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When performing abdominal paracentesis, take care to avoid puncturing intestine; be aware of common-harm concerns and adjust technique (site, needle/cannula size, angle) accordingly; document procedural precautions and observed complications or lack thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative reporting of volumes, weights, and counts
rubrics_metrics.description: The author records precise measures: e.g. 'about 3 gallons', 'to the number of 76 quarts, including the 3 gallons ... amount[s] to the quantity of 19 gallons', kidney stone 'weighing 1 an ounce'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide exact or best-estimate quantitative measurements (volumes of fluid evacuated, weights of calculi, counts of units) to support reproducibility and interpretation of pathological states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative description of colour, consistency, and texture
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed tissue/fluid descriptions: 'this humour... in colour and consistence somewhat resembled water, saving that it was of a somewhat deeper red, and had a more crass hypostasis'; organs 'looked all of them like flesh half boiled', 'the stomach contained nothing but wind, with which, like a blown bladder, it would return after the least impression.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include vivid qualitative descriptors of colour, consistency, and comparative similes for tissues and effusions to convey pathological appearance when illustrations are omitted or inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe anatomical attachments, vascular connections, and adhesions
rubrics_metrics.description: Anatomical detail example: 'when the author attempted to take it away, he found it still attached by a considerably firm pedicle, through which were transmitted blood-vessels to the ovum. It is by these blood-vessels... that the foetus receives its nourishment... this pedicle serving to form the placenta.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record presence/absence of pedicles, vessels, adhesions, and their relations to surrounding structures; note whether attachments could explain physiological/pathological processes (e.g., nourishment, placentation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparative (animal) observations to corroborate human findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative note: similar liquor found in sows' Fallopian tubes—'accordingly on opening a sow, the author found appearances similar to those observed in this woman... the Fallopian tubes... contained 3 or 4 ounces of the aforesaid liquor.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When available, report analogous findings from animals and discuss similarities/differences to human cases to strengthen anatomical or functional inferences; explicitly state when animal evidence corroborates or differs from human observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record clinical symptom patterns as diagnostic indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical signs linked to diagnoses: e.g. 'One of the great indications of this woman's pregnancy was a flux of a whitish humour to her breasts... She had likewise laboured... under a suppression of the menses.' And for kidney stone: 'loss of appetite and bad health... vomiting... a copious discharge of green bile by stool... could not be recruited... was unable to lie on either side, on account of the pain.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and correlate presenting symptoms (e.g., galactorrhea and amenorrhea for suspected pregnancy; vomiting, bilious stool, localized pain for renal colic/stone) with later anatomical or pathological findings; document temporal course and treatments tried.
